body:
What Will Kai Wear?: 1. A warm coat, a hat and mittens. 2. Shorts and a sun hat. 3. To drink, so Kai does not get too hot or thirsty. 4. They keep Kai's hands warm.
Dress for a Rainy Day: the drawing shows rain gear such as a rain coat, boots or an umbrella, and the told sentence names it ("I wear boots. I bring an umbrella.").
Hot Day or Cold Day?: 1. A cold day. 2. A hot day. 3. Mittens, the scarf and the warm coat. 4. 3 hot day things (shorts, sandals, sun hat). 5. Any cold day item, such as boots, a hat, a sweater or warm socks.
Dressed for the Weather Check: 1. Any two cold weather items (coat, hat, mittens, scarf, boots, snow pants). 2. Boots (rain boots). 3. A sun hat or cap. 4. Drawing shows warm clothes for snow. 5. The reason names warmth, for example "to stay warm" or "so my hands do not get cold".
Scoring tip: a student who chooses good clothes but cannot yet say why is Getting there on "I can tell why I picked them". A hat is right for both hot and cold days; accept it in either group if the student tells why.
title: Answer key: Dress for the Weather
